Dear Ms. Rivera,

I hope you're doing well. Living here for the past six months has been a real pleasure; the neighborhood is peaceful, and you have always been quick to help whenever something came up.

Unfortunately, I need to let you know that the kitchen faucet is still leaking. The repair worker you sent last Thursday tightened a few fittings, but he mentioned that the cartridge itself was cracked and that he would need to order a replacement. Since then, nobody has come back, and water is now dripping steadily into the cabinet under the sink. I've placed a towel and a container there, but I'm concerned the cabinet floor may start to warp.

Would it be possible to have the repair finished sometime this week? I work from home on Wednesdays and Fridays, so either of those days would be ideal, and I'd be happy to let the worker in at any time.

Thank you so much for looking into this.

Best regards,
Sofia

Dear Ms. Rivera,

I hope you are well. I really like living in this apartment, it is quiet and close to my work.

I am writing about the kitchen faucet. Last week a repair man came, but he did not finish. He said he need another part and he will come back, but he never came. Now the water is dripping into the cabinet under the sink and the bottom is getting wet.

Could you tell me when someone can fix it? I am usually at home after 5 p.m. on weekdays, so Monday or Tuesday evening would be good for me.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Kenji

I believe companies should adopt a four-day work week, although Mei is right that it cannot look the same in every industry. Building on Liam's point, the main benefit is not only rest but focus: when employees know they have one fewer day, they cut unnecessary meetings and prioritize work that matters. For example, my uncle's accounting firm moved to four ten-hour days, and its error rate dropped because staff were less exhausted by Friday. As for Mei's concern, hospitals and stores could rotate schedules so that each worker gets a three-day weekend while the business stays open every day. That is why I think a flexible four-day model makes sense for most companies.

In my opinion, companies should try a four-day work week. I agree with Liam that people come back more rested after a long weekend, and rested workers make less mistakes. For example, when I had a part-time job, I was always more careful on Monday after a good weekend. However, I understand Mei's point that stores and hospitals must open every day. But they could use shifts, so different workers take different days off. Overall, I think the advantages are bigger than the problems.
